meta.notes: Scope: EU DPP (ESPR) and battery passport demand on Indian/Asian SME suppliers, plus the adjacent CBAM data regime for steel. Most problem evidence is trade press and vendor/consultancy content (vendors have commercial interest); no survey of Indian SME suppliers' hours or questionnaire counts was found. Strongest contradictions: delegated acts for textiles/steel not adopted by mid/late 2026 (textile DPP ~2028-2029), first battery passport excludes carbon/recycled/due-diligence data, and 'enter once, share many' plus selective disclosure already exist (TrusTrace free supplier portal, Retraced, Higg FEM, Circularise, UNTP, EU O3CI). Unfetchable: SupplyChainBrain, GBA roundtable PDF, KPMG DPP survey PDF, apparelresources, cheqd. Prospects: only 11 companies for the primary ICP (EU brands with Asian supply chains), below the 20+ target; many brand sites were unfetchable (404/robots: Primark, Tom Tailor, Bestseller, H&M India pages, Indiska, Hessnatur). No battery or steel importers with India sourcing were found on fetchable own pages. Two leads (Jyoti, Lebenskleidung) are below the ICP size band; ARMEDANGELS and KnowledgeCotton have weak India evidence. Contacts only where name+title appear on the company's own page (4). icp_id null (context returned no ICP ids).

summary.statement: Textile suppliers report large per-request effort: one supplier said gathering data for a single order takes up to 15 days, and some factories are audited up to 200 times a year.

Vendors describe the multiplier from many buyers using different formats (a two-hour request becoming two days across ten buyers) and per-retailer assessments taking three to four weeks before a shared hub.
For DPP specifically, the cost is described as staff time to gather and update supplier figures, roughly half a role in an exporting SME; no measured hours from Indian SMEs were found.
No source counts how many DPP questionnaires an Indian or Asian SME receives per year.
Upstream suppliers mostly hold data in PDFs, spreadsheets and email, and EU buyers already send supplier questionnaires ahead of the delegated acts.
Supplier-side 'enter once, share with many' tools already exist: TrusTrace free supplier profiles, Higg FEM (300+ brands), Retraced's supplier network, and Indian services such as GreenSutra.
Indian exporters hold an estimated ~60% of textile DPP data; the gaps are upstream and granular (tier-2, batch-level, carbon), which is an engagement problem more than a data-entry one.
The legal duty sits with the EU economic operator (usually the importer/brand) and cannot be delegated, so the EU brand is the natural payer.
Guidance points to a cross-functional DPP team (sourcing, sustainability, IT, legal, finance) rather than a single budget owner.
No evidence of any budget allocated specifically to supplier data tools was found; brand-side vendors make the supplier side free.

Battery buyers face a hard 18 Feb 2027 deadline and only 15% of surveyed companies were very confident value-chain data would be ready; buyers push data warranties into contracts and may replace slow suppliers.

For textiles, steel, aluminium and tyres no delegated act was adopted by mid/late 2026; textile DPPs are expected around 2028-2029, and the first battery passport excludes carbon footprint, recycled content and due diligence data.
Adjacent CBAM data demands are already costing some Indian steel exporters small EU buyers.
Shared single-assessment models show value: One Retail Hub reports ~70% time savings and Higg FEM is shared across 300+ brands.
But the same value is already offered free or near-free by incumbents and open standards (TrusTrace, Retraced, Higg, UNTP), weakening the idea's claim that brand-side vendors neglect suppliers.
No direct evidence on Indian SME suppliers' willingness to pay INR 1,000-5,000/month was found.

Buyers and regulators look for third-party verification: chain-of-custody certificates from credentialed bodies, EU-accredited verifiers for CBAM values, and approved Higg FEM verifiers whose results can be reused.
The EU registry only checks format and completeness, leaving data credibility to operators and market surveillance.
Digital credential schemes for this already exist (UNTP conformity credentials, EBSI/TRACE4EU pilot).

Suppliers fear transparency exposes them to competitors and brand price pressure; competitive concerns have slowed battery data sharing; Indian steel MSMEs worry about disclosing supplier, cost and production data.
Battery passport figures that were bilateral become public via QR, and exporters are advised to protect trade secrets and limit BOM disclosure in DPP clauses.
Selective disclosure is already offered by Circularise, the open UNTP standard and the EU's O3CI module for steel.

hypothesis_update.problem: EU brands and importers must collect DPP and battery-passport data that only non-EU suppliers hold; Asian SME suppliers answer repeated, differently formatted buyer requests by spreadsheet and email, lack upstream (tier-2, batch, carbon) data, and fear exposing commercially sensitive figures. Hard deadlines exist only for batteries (Feb 2027) and CBAM steel data; textile/steel DPPs are expected 2028-2029.
hypothesis_update.users: Indian and other Asian SME exporters (batteries/LMT packs, textiles and apparel, steel and metal parts) supplying EU brands and importers.
hypothesis_update.buyer: EU brands and importers, who carry the non-delegable legal duty; suppliers are unlikely to pay because comparable supplier portals are free.
hypothesis_update.decision_maker: Cross-functional DPP owners at EU brands (sourcing, sustainability, compliance), with no single evidenced budget owner.
hypothesis_update.economic_value: Time saved on repeated supplier requests (shared-assessment hubs report ~70% savings), faster qualification for EU orders, and protection of sensitive data; but incumbents offer this free or near-free.
hypothesis_update.geography: Suppliers in India and Asia; buyers in the European Union.
hypothesis_update.industry: Batteries, textiles and apparel, steel and metal parts supply chains.

rationale.statement: Battery deadline is fixed while textile/steel DPP acts are not yet adopted.
Legal duty sits with the EU operator and cannot be delegated.

new_unknowns.question: Do Indian SME suppliers serving several EU buyers face buyers on different platforms (TrusTrace, Retraced, Circularise, Higg) such that a neutral credential wallet still saves time, or has one platform per sector already won?
Will EU brands pay per onboarded supplier when TrusTrace, Retraced and Higg make the supplier side free?
Which battery/LMT and steel exporters in India actually receive EU passport or CBAM data requests today, and how many per year?

current_solutions.statement: Most upstream suppliers answer buyer requests with PDFs, spreadsheets and email, in each buyer's own format.
Brands onboard suppliers onto brand-side platforms (TrusTrace, Retraced) whose supplier side is free and reusable across brands.
Industry shared assessments (Higg FEM) already let facilities complete once and share verified results with many brands.
Indian exporters buy help from consultancies and DPP partners (GreenSutra, GreenStitch) or join association-led pilots (PDEXCIL-AWARE).
